name: Two-stream station: recycle and trash
local_rules: This station has NO compost bin. Everything that is not recyclable and not special goes to TRASH.

RECYCLE (blue, left) takes: empty plastic bottles, jugs and tubs marked 1 (PET/PETE), 2 (HDPE) or 5 (PP), caps on; aluminum and steel cans; clean foil; empty glass bottles and jars; clean dry paper and cardboard (boxes, newspaper, office paper, mail, paper bags, clean pizza boxes); empty milk and juice cartons.
Recycling must be EMPTY: no liquid and no chunks of food. A thin film or a few drops left behind is fine, nobody needs to wash anything.
RECYCLE never takes: plastic bags or film, foam, greasy or wet paper, paper cups, utensils, straws, chip bags, anything with food still in it.

TRASH (black, right) takes: food scraps; greasy or food-stained paper including greasy pizza boxes, used napkins and paper plates; compostable cups and utensils (there is no compost here); plastic bags, film and wrappers; chip bags and candy wrappers; foam; plastic utensils and straws; paper cups and their lids; plastics marked 3, 4, 6 or 7; tied bags of mixed trash; broken glass or ceramics; anything that cannot be pulled apart.
A pizza box: greasy, cheesy or with food stuck to it goes to TRASH. Completely clean goes to RECYCLE.

Mold, rot or wetness: moldy or rotten food is still food and goes to TRASH; paper or cardboard that is moldy, rotten or wet can never be recycled and goes to TRASH as well, however little of it is affected.

A clear plastic cup cannot be told apart from the side: marked '1 PETE' it is RECYCLE; marked 'compostable' or 'PLA' it is TRASH (no compost here). The mark is usually on the underside, so ask to see the bottom. When the cup really carries no mark, or the person will not show it, it is TRASH.

LIQUIDS never go into any bin. Leftover drink gets poured out first (sink or drain), then the container is sorted by its material. If the person cannot empty it, the container goes to TRASH with the cap on.
Food inside a container: food goes to TRASH, then the container is sorted by its material.

SPECIAL, never in any of these bins: batteries of every kind and anything with a battery inside (vapes, phones, earbuds, toys) go to the battery or e-waste drop-off because they start fires; electronics, cables and light bulbs go to e-waste; needles go to a sharps container; medication goes to a pharmacy take-back; paint, chemicals, lighters, propane and any aerosol can that is not completely empty go to the hazardous waste drop-off. A completely empty aerosol can is RECYCLE.
Things that are not trash (keys, wallets, working devices someone is just holding, clothes or books in good shape) should not be binned: say so, and suggest keeping or donating.

When the facts cannot be established, choose the answer that does no harm whichever way the truth turns out; if none exists, TRASH. A wrong item in recycling spoils the whole load, a recyclable in the trash does not.
